ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 3, $\angle BDC = 120^\circ$, $BD = CD$, points M and N are located on sides $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, and $\angle MDN = 60^\circ$. Connecting $MN$, what is the perimeter of $\triangle AMN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $AB$ to $F$ such that $BF=CN$, connect $DF$, \\
$\because$ $\triangle BDC$ is an isosceles triangle, $\angle BDC=120^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BCD=\angle DBC=30^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with side length of 3, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle BAC=\angle BCA=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBA=\angle DCA=90^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle DBF$ and $\triangle CND$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}BF=CN \\ \angle DBF=\angle DCN \\ DB=DC\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BDF\cong \triangle CDN\left(SAS\right)$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDF=\angle CDN$, $DF=DN$, \\
$\because$ $\angle MDN=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDM+\angle CDN=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDM+\angle BDF=60^\circ=\angle FDM=\angle MDN$, \\
In $\triangle DMN$ and $\triangle DMF$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}DN=DF \\ \angle MDN=\angle MDF \\ DM=MD\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DMN\cong \triangle DMF\left(SAS\right)$, \\
$\therefore$ $MN=MF$, \\
$\therefore$ $MF=BF+BM=BM+CN=MN$, \\
$\therefore$ The perimeter of $\triangle AMN$ $AM+AN+MN=AM+MB+BF+AN=AB+AN+CN=AB+AC=\boxed{6}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with side length 3, $\angle BDC = 120^\circ$, $BD = CD$, points $M$ and $N$ are on sides $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, and $\angle MDN = 60^\circ$. Connect $MN$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle AMN$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $AB$ to $F$ such that $BF=CN$, and connect $DF$. \\
$\because$ $\triangle BDC$ is isosceles and $\angle BDC=120^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BCD=\angle DBC=30^\circ$. \\
$\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with side length 3, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle BAC=\angle BCA=60^\circ$. \\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBA=\angle DCA=90^\circ$. \\
In $\triangle DBF$ and $\triangle CND$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}BF=CN \\ \angle DBF=\angle DCN \\ DB=DC\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BDF\cong \triangle CDN\,(SAS)$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDF=\angle CDN$, and $DF=DN$. \\
$\because$ $\angle MDN=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDM+\angle CDN=60^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDM+\angle BDF=60^\circ=\angle FDM=\angle MDN$. \\
In $\triangle DMN$ and $\triangle DMF$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}DN=DF \\ \angle MDN=\angle MDF \\ DM=MD\end{array}\right.$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DMN\cong \triangle DMF\,(SAS)$, \\
$\therefore$ $MN=MF$. \\
$\therefore$ $MF=BF+BM=BM+CN=MN$. \\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle AMN$ is \\
$AM+AN+MN=AM+MB+BF+AN=AB+AN+CN=AB+AC=\boxed{6}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: As can be seen from the attached figure, A is the upper vertex, B and C are respectively at the lower left and lower right, forming triangle ABC; D is located below BC, DB and DC have been connected; M is on side AB, N is on side AC, and DM, DN, and MN are also connected in the figure. Reasoning: It is known that ABC is an equilateral triangle with side length 3, so ∠ABC=∠BCA=∠BAC=60°. Also BD=CD and ∠BDC=120°, therefore the base angles of triangle BDC are ∠DBC=∠BCD=(180°-120°)/2=30°. Thus DB is perpendicular to AB, and DC is perpendicular to AC. According to the auxiliary point method, extend AB outward through B to point F, make BF=CN, and connect DF. Because DB=DC, BF=CN, and ∠DBF=∠DCN=90°, triangle DBF and triangle DCN are congruent by SAS. Therefore DF=DN, and ∠BDF=∠CDN. Since ∠BDC=120°, while ∠MDN=60°, and M and N are located in the internal connecting-line position, the remaining angles on the two sides satisfy ∠BDM+∠CDN=60°. Also ∠CDN=∠BDF, therefore ∠BDM+∠BDF=60°, that is, ∠FDM=∠MDN. Now look at triangles DFM and DNM: DF=DN, DM is a common side, and the included angle ∠FDM=∠MDN, so the two are congruent by SAS, obtaining MF=MN. Since F is on the extension of AB through B, and A, M, B, F are collinear, MF=MB+BF=MB+CN. Therefore the perimeter of triangle AMN is AM+AN+MN=AM+AN+MB+CN=(AM+MB)+(AN+CN)=AB+AC=3+3=6.
